RQ2/RQ6: B3 and B2 both cut the probe's dispatch latency by about 3-4 orders of magnitude against B0/B1 and raise I/O throughput about 24x, for at most about 1.2 % less batch throughput (B3 vs B0 in the mixed scenario; B1 has CV 11 %). B3 does NOT clearly beat the hand-picked B2: p99 84 vs 104 µs in the mixed scenario but 142 vs 52 µs in the batch scenario, with CV 38-62 %. The adaptive policy's value is that it reaches B2-level behaviour without being told the workload, not that it beats the best fixed policy. Wake latency p50 (979 µs vs 30 ms) contains the tick-phase offset of this boot (F-117).

RQ5: partly yes. The adaptive cache detects the sequential stream and matches the dedicated read-ahead policy (97 % of its throughput, 15.8x LRU), it is the best policy on random (21.02 MB/s) and within 8 % of the best on scan (26.87 vs 29.18). It is 18 % below LRU and 22 % below CLOCK on the hotset workload, so on re-use workloads it does not pick the best fixed policy. Hotset results vary between runs (LRU 75.32 here vs 87.82 in E-114) and there are only 2 repetitions. No extra memory: all policies use the same 1024 blocks.

RQ4: the system class follows each phase change within 284-401 ms, which is 2-4 profiler windows (100 ms window, hysteresis 2) plus the 250 ms sampling interval of the benchmark. The earlier 4.4-5.7 s outlier (F-115) is gone. Phases were 8 s, not the 60 s of NEW_EXPLANATION §36, to keep the campaign short; the measured delays are far below 8 s.

E-120: Mixed scenario, median of 3. Dispatch p50 / p99 (µs): A1 controller off 29,058 / 30,051; A2 profiling off 11,205 / 17,062; A3 profiling on, no switching 29,057 / 29,341; A4 adaptive 6 / 56; A5 adaptive + adaptive cache 6 / 71; A6 window 25 ms 6 / 60; A6 window 500 ms 6 / 14,042; A7 hysteresis 1 7 / 77; A7 hysteresis 5 6 / 11,990. Batch jobs/s (x100) 954,234-985,723 in all variants. Policy decision time A3 67,255 ns/s, A4 138,256 ns/s. Profiler total for the whole boot: 8.86 ms.

RQ1/RQ3: the latency gain needs both profiling and class-based parameters. Profiling alone (A3) changes nothing; the adaptive policy without profiles (A2, every task UNKNOWN) is in between. The adaptive cache (A5) does not change scheduler metrics in this scenario (random I/O). Reaction speed matters: a 500 ms window or hysteresis 5 raises dispatch p99 about 210-250x, because new threads start UNKNOWN and wait behind CPU workers until classified; 25 ms vs 100 ms windows make no measurable difference. Overhead: the profiler used 8.86 ms in a boot of at least 270 s of benchmarks (< 0.004 % of CPU); policy decisions under A4 cost about 0.14 ms per second (0.014 %). The larger cost is about 9x more context switches than round-robin (visible in E-117), which is not in these numbers.
Measure context-switch cost directly; per-class initial placement for new threads.
